messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] range of Posterior mean spatial random field
parts:
On Mon, 2019-07-01 at 13:39 -0700, Eliecerecology wrote:
> Hi,
> I am new using INLA, I have run the following model:
>
> f2 <- y ~ -1 + Intercept + f(sal0.std, model = "rw2") + f(temp10.std,
> model = "rw2") + sec.std + f(w, model = spde)

I would suggest to add scale.model=TRUE to the rw2 models, to put them
on the same scale; see

http://www.r-inla.org/examples/tutorials/tutorial-on-option-scale-model


>
> I2 <- inla(f2,
> family = "poisson",
> data = inla.stack.data(StackFit),
> control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, config =
> TRUE),
> control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(StackFit)),
> verbose = FALSE)
>
> However I am not sure of the posterior random field obtained since
> values ranges from 0.8 to 2.4, is there a specific constrain for this
> range?

there is no constraint for the range. It might be you want to use the
PC-priors for the SPDE to excplicite control the marginal stddev; see

http://www.r-inla.org/spde-book

and the gitbook

> I have also run the model above using the family "nbinomial", but
> instead of reduce the dispersion, it increases it 10 folds.

I guess you're using a to complex model for the data you have. You can
control the overdispersion as described in inla.doc("nbinomial")




> Is this sound familiar? is there a way to specify the "dispersion
> parameter" of neg. binomial distribution in INLA?
>
> Thanks,
> Eliecer
